author: Ethan Dahlen
title: Dupont Hospital to see birthplace expansion, growing population trend - NewsBreak
text:
By Ethan Dahlen ,
1 hours ago FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE) — “We create a little city every month”
That’s how Dupont Hospital CEO Brent Parsons describes the booming birth rate Lutheran Health Network is seeing in Fort Wayne. June was a record 282 births for the hospital, and the Dupont Hospital Birthplace facility sees about 3,000 births each year.
“Every month’s different. You know, depending on what happened, you know, 9, 10 months before that, but every month’s different. We don’t see, we don’t expect that every single month, but we have to be able to accommodate at least that much, if not more, in any given month,” Parsons said.
A sign just outside the Birthplace. That uptick is the cause for a major renovation and expansion in the Birthplace that will begin this summer. Beginning August 3 and lasting up to a year, Lutheran says the renovation “will increase the Birthplace’s capacity while creating a more modern, comfortable, and family-centered environment for growing families.”
The Birthplace will remain open during construction, and normal capacity should not be affected. New rooms will be built before the old ones are modernized, allowing families to use the newest rooms while the older ones are updated.
“So aesthetically, the entire unit we have a labor unit and a postpartum unit that are connected. The entire unit is going to be renovated and look completely different. Look more modern. Have new flooring, new paint, new lighting, new cabinetry throughout. And then also, there’s some area that’s going to be renovated that’s not well-purposed right now,” Parsons said. “We’re going to add two new labor rooms so that we can add two new laboring moms. So that moms that come, every mom who comes that’s in labor, will have a room that’s fully renovated and refurbished to be able to accommodate them.”
A rendering that shows what the new rooms at the Birthplace will look like. As Lutheran has closed similar childbirth centers at Bluffton Regional Medical Center in Bluffton and Dukes Memorial Hospital in Peru, WANE 15 asked whether that was also a factor in the uptick in activity on Dupont Road.
It seems that part of the uptick in demand at Dupont is linked to the closure of those other centers, as well as to a rapidly growing Summit City.
“We’ve seen that because of what you mentioned, but also with the Fort Wayne population just continuing growing. We’re having more and more people move here, and we want to be that premier birthing site in Northeast Indiana for them,” Parsons said.
Navigating the parking lot may be affected for the duration of the renovation and expansion.
